title: Cognitive Labor vs Emotional Labor: What's the Difference?
dek: Cognitive labor and emotional labor get lumped together, but they're not the same. Here's the difference, with real examples, and why you're probably doing both.

title: 50 Things on the Mental Load Nobody Sees
dek: Real mental load examples, 50 of them, the invisible planning and remembering that never makes it onto a to-do list. If you carry these, you're not imagining it.

title: How to Stop Being the Default Parent (Without Just Doing It All Yourself)
dek: Asking for help keeps you the manager. Here's how to hand off whole areas of the mental load, so someone else actually remembers them.

title: The Lunchbox Isn't a Cooking Problem. It's a Decision Problem.
dek: Packing lunch isn't hard because you're disorganized. It's hard because it asks you to decide the same thing fresh, every morning, before coffee. Here's the fix that isn't a better lunch.

title: Why Travel Is Where the Mental Load Gets Loud
dek: At home the mental load is spread thin enough to ignore. On a trip, all of it comes due at once. Here's why, and the one habit that actually helps.

title: You Can't Fix Summer
dek: There's a part of summer no printable will fix. There's also a part you're carrying that you don't have to carry the same way.

title: Summer Break Is a Luxury Tax on Parents — Especially the Ones Doing It Alone
dek: The mental load doesn't go away when school ends. For some families it shifts. For others, it breaks them. Both deserve to be named.

title: What is "mental load," and why does naming it actually matter?
dek: Everyone talks about it. Fewer people can explain it. Here's what the research says — and why being seen matters more than being helped.

title: Why apps don't fix the mental load — and what would actually help
dek: Shared calendars move the information. They don't move the responsibility. That distinction is everything.

title: How to show your partner what you're actually managing (without it becoming a fight)
dek: The problem isn't that they don't care. It's that they can't see it. Here's how to make the invisible visible.
